control_title: Disable SMBv1 and require SMB signing
text: Legacy SMBv1 should be disabled on all Windows hosts, as it lacks modern security controls and is the protocol version targeted by well-known remote code execution exploits. SMB signing should be required to prevent relay and tampering attacks. Disable SMBv1 via PowerShell (Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol) or Group Policy, and verify no legacy applications depend on it before rollout.

control_title: Apply security updates for SMB remote code execution vulnerabilities promptly
text: Hosts exposing SMB services should be patched against known remote code execution vulnerabilities as a priority, since SMB is a common lateral-movement and ransomware entry vector. Maintain a patch cadence that applies critical SMB-related security updates within 72 hours of release for internet- or high-value-network-facing systems.

control_title: Restrict RDP exposure and enforce Network Level Authentication
text: Remote Desktop Protocol should not be exposed directly to untrusted networks. Where RDP is required, enforce Network Level Authentication (NLA), require multi-factor authentication, and restrict access via firewall rules or a VPN/bastion host rather than direct internet exposure. Unrestricted RDP exposure is one of the most common initial access vectors in ransomware incidents.

Anonymous FTP login should be disabled unless there is an explicit, documented business requirement for public unauthenticated file access. Anonymous access allows any network-reachable client to list directories and, depending on configuration, upload or retrieve files without accountability. Where FTP is required at all, prefer SFTP/FTPS with authenticated access.

control_title: Keep database engine patched against authentication bypass vulnerabilities
text: Database servers should run supported, patched versions of the database engine. Older MySQL/MariaDB versions have contained authentication bypass vulnerabilities that allow login without correct credentials under certain conditions. Apply vendor security patches promptly and avoid running end-of-life database versions in production.

control_title: Restrict database network exposure to application tiers only
text: Database services should not be reachable from general user networks or the internet. Bind the database to internal interfaces only and use firewall rules or security groups to restrict inbound connections to the specific application servers that require access.

control_title: Monitor and renew TLS certificates before expiry
text: TLS certificates should be tracked with automated expiry monitoring and renewed well before their expiration date. An expired certificate causes client trust warnings or hard connection failures, and in some client configurations, silently downgrades security expectations. Automated renewal (e.g. via ACME/Let's Encrypt or enterprise PKI tooling) is preferred over manual tracking.

control_title: Keep web server software on a supported, patched version
text: Web server software should be kept current with vendor security patches, and end-of-life versions should be upgraded. Older Apache httpd releases have accumulated known vulnerabilities that are fixed in later maintenance branches; running an outdated version increases exposure without proportionate benefit.

control_title: Disable password authentication in favor of key-based SSH login
text: SSH should be configured to disable password authentication and require public-key authentication instead, reducing exposure to credential-stuffing and brute-force attacks. Combine this with disabling root login over SSH and restricting access to specific source networks where feasible.

Redis should require a password via the requirepass directive for all access. A Redis instance bound to the network with no password allows any reachable client to read, modify, or destroy all data and, in some configurations, run Lua scripts. If Redis is not required to be network-exposed, bind it to loopback only.

control_title: Restrict Redis network exposure and enable protected-mode
text: Redis protected-mode should stay enabled and the server should bind to internal interfaces only, so the database cannot be reached from untrusted networks. Where remote access is required, place it behind a bastion/VPN rather than direct exposure.

MongoDB should run with authorization enabled. Instances started without --auth accept every connection as the all-powerful role and expose every collection to any reachable client — a pattern behind several large-scale data breaches.

control_title: Bind MongoDB to internal interfaces only
text: MongoDB should bind to 127.0.0.1 or internal interfaces, never 0.0.0.0 on a public network. Use firewall rules or security groups to restrict inbound database traffic to the application tier.
